case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
**Pick: Grand Haven pier.** I'd rate pier fishing this week as slow to average at best. The recent reports are all from boats, so these ratings are my own inference.

| Port | Pier rating (0–4) |
|---|---|
| **Grand Haven** | **2** (average, with upside if the cold water holds) |
| Muskegon | 2 (same signal as Grand Haven, but I have no pier history for it) |
| South Haven | 1 (below average) |
| St. Joseph | 1 (below average) |

**What the reports say**
- The newest report is 6 days old (2025-07-30). No 2025 report I pulled covers pier salmon fishing, only boats.
- Boats did well off Grand Haven and Muskegon. Both were rated good (3), with fish 50–90 ft down at Grand Haven and 60–100 ft down at Muskegon, in 100–160 ft of water. Glow plugs, meat rigs and rotator/fly combos worked at both, and glow spoons also worked at Muskegon (Grand Haven and Muskegon, 2025-07-30).
- South Haven was also rated good (3) for Chinook in about 95–115 ft of water, mostly on spoons. Coho were rated 1 (South Haven, 2025-07-30).
- St. Joseph was rated average (2), with fish spread out from 90 ft to well beyond 110 ft (St. Joseph, 2025-07-30).
- Fish were in deep water. None of these reports say salmon were near the piers.
- The surface-water summary for the week before today shows sharp drops, which is the upwelling sign:

| Port | Buoy surface temperature | Change over the week |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Haven and Muskegon | avg 67 F | -14 F |
| South Haven | avg 65 F | -9 F |
| St. Joseph | avg 69 F | -4 F |

- Before the drop, buoy temperatures were 75–77 F.

**History (earlier seasons, early to mid August)**
- Pier fishing for salmon was usually slow even when boats were doing well:
  - Grand Haven: slow in 2023-08-16, "a few" salmon in 2023-08-02, and a few coho in 2022-08-17.
  - St. Joseph: slow in 2024-07-31, a few coho on nightcrawlers in 2023-08-09, and mostly steelhead with a few Chinook in 2022-08-17.
- South Haven piers were closed for several days by red flag conditions in 2022-08-10, so check for closures there.

**General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension)**
- North or east winds push warm surface water offshore, and cold water wells up along the shore. That brings salmon toward pierheads.

**My read**
- I'd expect the big temperature drops at Grand Haven and Muskegon to be the best chance of salmon moving in close. That is why I put Grand Haven and Muskegon above the other two.
- Past upwelling weeks at the piers still produced only slow to below-average fishing, so I wouldn't go above 2.
- St. Joseph's smaller drop and its steelhead-heavy pier history put it at the bottom.
- If you go, I'd fish early or late in low light. Glow spoons and glow plugs are the lures the reports tie to low-light or shallower bites.

**Caveats**
- Live conditions weren't available. I got only the weekly buoy summary, with no pierhead water temperatures, cold-layer depths or wind forecast. Check the wind and any pier closures before you go.
- The drops are measured at buoys miles offshore, so they don't confirm what the water is doing at the pier.
